outcome: The standard conjectures in general remain open. Since 26 January 2024 partial results have appeared for abelian varieties and their powers (Agugliaro 2024 and 2025; Broe, August 2026, which claims to complete the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds; Li, September 2026, partly withdrawn), and an unrefereed OpenAI manuscript dated 30 September 2026 and released 6 October 2026 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, from which its catalogue derives the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic via Milne's theorems; none of this reaches the general conjectures.
problem_asks: The bullet asks about the standard conjectures on algebraic cycles, taken as Wikipedia's article enumerates them (the frozen bullet itself is just the title). (1) Conjecture A, equivalent to B per Wikipedia: the Lefschetz-type statement that Lefschetz operators from hard Lefschetz on a smooth hyperplane section are induced by algebraic cycles (Conjecture B as Wikipedia words it). (2) Conjecture C, Kunneth type: the Kunneth projectors H*(X) to H^i(X) to H*(X) are induced by algebraic cycles with rational coefficients. (3) Conjecture D: numerical and homological equivalence of algebraic cycles coincide. (4) The Hodge standard conjecture, modelled on the Hodge index theorem: the cup-product pairing on primitive algebraic classes has the predicted definiteness (sign). Each is a claim about all smooth projective varieties over the relevant field. The statement names all of them together, so settling the bullet requires all four; settling any one leaves the others open. Wikipedia's own status lines: the Hodge standard conjecture is true over C but largely unknown over finite fields; Conjecture C is known over finite fields but largely unknown over C; Conjecture D is known for abelian varieties in the Clozel case, for infinitely many primes l.

events.what_happened: Grothendieck's 1958 result proving the Hodge-type standard conjecture for surfaces in positive characteristic, as cited by the Wikipedia article. I did not open the original.
events.delivers: Hodge-type standard conjecture for smooth projective surfaces in positive characteristic (per Wikipedia's summary).
events.remains: The Hodge-type statement in dimension three and above, and Conjectures B, C, D in general.
events.direction: Confirms the Hodge-type conjecture in the surface case, so it cuts in the conjectured direction.

events.what_happened: Lieberman's work on the standard conjectures for abelian varieties. The Wikipedia article attributes to Lieberman (1968) the complex-case Conjecture D for dimension at most four and for abelian varieties; a Milne article snippet credits Lieberman (1968) and Kleiman (1968) with the Lefschetz standard conjecture for abelian varieties; a 2026 arXiv snippet credits him with the Lefschetz and Kunneth types. The attribution is not settled by the sources I read. I did not open Lieberman's paper.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia: Conjecture D over C for varieties of dimension at most four and for abelian varieties. Per the Milne snippet: the Lefschetz standard conjecture for abelian varieties. Which of these Lieberman established is unresolved here.
events.remains: Over C, the Hodge-type statement beyond these cases; over finite fields and in positive characteristic, the general conjectures.
events.doubts: The attribution differs between the Wikipedia article and the snippets I saw; I did not read Lieberman's paper, which would settle which conjecture it proves.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction for the abelian and low-dimensional cases.

events.what_happened: Ancona, Standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds, arXiv:1806.03216, first posted 8 June 2018 (v1), later revisions 5 Sep 2018 and 2 Sep 2020. Proves the Hodge-type standard conjecture for an abelian fourfold A (characteristic p, per the published abstract as shown in search). The published version appeared in Inventiones Mathematicae; the arXiv comment says 'Final version, published online in Inventiones Mathematicae' and that the p-adic part was improved after the referee's ideas. Wikipedia (frozen Jan 2024) dates this to 2020; the first public written argument is the 2018 preprint.

events.delivers: The Hodge-type standard conjecture for every abelian fourfold A (characteristic p, per the published abstract). Combined with a theorem of Clozel, numerical equivalence equals l-adic homological equivalence on A for infinitely many primes l. The arXiv abstract I read does not state the characteristic; the published abstract does.
events.remains: The Hodge-type conjecture for abelian varieties of dimension other than four in general; Conjecture D on abelian fourfolds for all l, which the paper's conclusion names as the remaining gap (l-independence of l-adic homological equivalence); Conjectures B and C are not claimed here.

The v1 abstract also claimed the Hodge standard conjecture for all smooth projective varieties if the Tate conjecture holds over finite fields; the published version keeps only the abelian-variety statement.

For hyper-Kahler manifolds the Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 2 is implied by the SYZ conjecture in the Lagrangian-fibration case, and is proved for Lagrangian covered fourfolds with rho(X)=1 and X general in moduli.

For varieties over finite fields with a CM lifting (abelian varieties, products of K3 surfaces), the signature predicted by the Hodge standard conjecture holds modulo 4; this needs the discriminant (from l-adic arguments) and the Hilbert symbol (from p-adic Hodge theory). events.what_happened: Truong, Standard conjecture D and some conjectures around Weil's Riemann hypothesis, arXiv:2508.13882 (v1 19 Aug 2025; v5 8 Dec 2025). Proves a conditional result: if Standard conjecture D holds for algebraic cycles of dimension dim X on X x X, then all polarised endomorphisms of X are semisimple. Also gives heuristic arguments that D should imply the dynamical degree comparison and norm comparison conjectures.
events.revisions: v1 19 Aug 2025; v2 25 Aug; v3 2 Sep; v4 15 Sep; v5 8 Dec 2025.

events.what_happened: Agugliaro, Examples for the standard conjecture of Hodge type, arXiv:2401.17445 (v1 30 Jan 2024; v2 13 Nov 2025). Constructs, for each prime p and each integer g (see note), infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p satisfying the Hodge-type standard conjecture, using Honda-Tate theory and a theorem of Ancona on rank-2 motives. The examples have Tate classes that are neither generated by divisors nor liftable to characteristic zero. Published Documenta Mathematica vol. 31 (2026), pp. 855-904, DOI 10.4171/DM/1057; EMS lists the published date as 19 January 2026.
events.revisions: v1 30 Jan 2024 (first public version, four days after the frozen revision); v2 13 Nov 2025 (current, accepted in Documenta Mathematica).
events.delivers: Instances: for each prime p and each g >= 4 (per the v2 HTML and the EMS abstract), infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p satisfying the Hodge-type standard conjecture. The arXiv abstract page I read gives g >= 5 instead; see doubts.
events.remains: The Hodge-type conjecture for all abelian varieties and all varieties; Conjectures B, C, D in general; the examples do not exhaust any class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published; EMS journal page lists 'Published' 19 January 2026, Vol. 31, No. 4

Taken together I read g >= 4 as current, but this is unresolved. The construction is explicit (Honda-Tate); I did not verify it.
events.direction: Instances of the Hodge-type standard conjecture for a class of abelian varieties; cuts in the conjectured direction.
events.object: Infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p, for each prime p and each g in the stated range, built explicitly by Honda-Tate theory; they satisfy the Hodge-type standard conjecture and carry Tate classes not generated by divisors nor liftable to characteristic zero.

events.what_happened: Agugliaro, Standard conjecture of Hodge type for powers of abelian varieties, arXiv:2510.21562 (single version, 24 Oct 2025). Abstract: proves the standard conjecture of Hodge type for powers of abelian threefolds; also for powers of simple abelian varieties over finite fields of prime dimension (Theorem 1.2: over F-bar_p), and related cases based on Lenstra-Zarhin Frobenius rank. Main tool: a comparison of two real fiber functors on Tannakian categories; second tool: an explicit description of simple Lefschetz motives over finite fields via enriched Frobenius eigenvalues.
events.revisions: v1 24 Oct 2025 only.
events.delivers: The Hodge-type standard conjecture for all powers of abelian threefolds (stated in the abstract; base field not given in the abstract), and for powers of simple abelian varieties of prime dimension over F-bar_p, plus related cases.
events.remains: Powers of abelian varieties of other dimensions and types; the general Hodge-type standard conjecture; Conjectures B, C, D in general.
events.direction: Partial positive results for abelian varieties; cuts in the conjectured direction.

events.what_happened: Foster, The Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4d-dimensional Kummer-type hyper-Kahler varieties, arXiv:2512.04114 (single version, 1 Dec 2025). Contingent upon a conjecture of Buchweitz and Flenner, proves the Lefschetz standard conjectures for projective varieties of generalized Kummer deformation type of dimension 4d.
events.revisions: v1 1 Dec 2025 only.

events.what_happened: Broe, The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields, arXiv:2608.28651 (v1 19 Aug 2026; single version). Abstract: proves the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields; combined with theorems of Ancona and Kahn, the standard conjecture on homological versus numerical equivalence holds for abelian fourfolds over arbitrary fields; with Lieberman and Ancona, 'completes the proof of the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds' (Corollary 1.2). The method reduces to Markman's results on algebraicity of Weil classes on complex abelian varieties. Acknowledges G. Ancona. Contains an LLM-use disclosure (see ai).
events.revisions: v1 19 Aug 2026 only.
events.delivers: For abelian fourfolds A: the Tate conjecture over finite fields (Theorem 1.1, every codimension via l-adic cycle class surjectivity over k, per the paper); Conjecture D for abelian fourfolds over arbitrary fields (via Ancona and Kahn); and, with Lieberman and Ancona, all of the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.2). Restricted to abelian fourfolds; the abstract claims completion of the standard conjectures for that class only.
events.remains: The standard conjectures for abelian varieties of dimension other than four and for all other smooth projective varieties; the general Tate and Hodge standard conjectures.
events.doubts: Single-author preprint, not refereed, posted 55 days before this record. My searches found no news, blog or expert commentary on it; the two Li preprints below cite it as established. The completion claim rests on Markman's Weil-class results, Ancona's theorem and a theorem of Kahn which I did not check, and on the author's own assessment (the paper's wording). The LLM disclosure does not state which parts of the argument were produced by the model beyond the sentences quoted in ai.
events.direction: Claims completion of the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds; for the class of abelian fourfolds the claimed result cuts in the conjectured direction.

systems.name: a large language model (unnamed; the author declines to identify it)
systems.what_it_did: The author states the model was used to explore proof strategies, locate relevant literature, critically examine mathematical arguments, and assist with copyediting and LaTeX typesetting. The author asked the model to attempt to use Markman's results to prove Theorem 1.1; the model suggested a method involving Ancona's analysis of exotic classes and the 'stabilization' idea discussed in Remark 1.4. The author then developed and restructured the strategy, identified and corrected errors and gaps, based the proof on Chow motives and devised a motivic technique that simplified the last step. The author says the text was composed by the author and all mathematical statements and references were independently checked. The source names no model; the author declined to name it, so the system is recorded here as described.
systems.basis_quote: The author initially asked the model to attempt to use Markman's results to prove Theorem 1.1, and proposed technical directions that a solution could take; in the ensuing interaction, the model suggested a method involving Ancona's analysis of exotic classes and the 'stabilization' idea discussed in Remark 1.4.

The author's withdrawal note says the manuscript will not be pursued as a standalone publication and selected methods will go into a separate paper.

Abstract: proves the Tate conjecture in every codimension on every power of an abelian variety of dimension at most four over a finite field; proves the Hodge conjecture for every power of a complex CM abelian fourfold (via Markman's theorem on Weil classes and Milne's criterion); states that the finite-field results imply standard conjecture D and the expected pole orders of the zeta function on every power. Acknowledgements disclose OpenAI Codex use (see ai). Section 11.2 says the results there follow from Broe's theorem on standard conjecture D.

Conditional on Broe's theorem for the D statement in Section 11.2, as the paper's text says; the body of the paper was only partly read.

I did not find that the note refers to the OpenAI CM Hodge manuscript; the abstract does not mention OpenAI. No outside engagement found.

The contribution to the main theorems is not stated, and I did not read the body of the paper, so I cannot say whether it is load-bearing.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', dated 30 September 2026 in the paper's README and folder name, released publicly in the openai/math repository on 6 October 2026 as part of a release of 722 manuscripts (372 families). Catalogue entry Family 032 (per CONTENTS.md, dated 6 Oct 2026): 'the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic' and 'the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields' are listed as consequences. Per secondary coverage (OfficeChai, not opened in full; search snippets), Theorem 1.1 states that every rational Hodge class on a complex CM abelian variety, in every codimension, is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes. The paper is authored by OpenAI with no named human authors. Not peer reviewed. Not Lean-formalized according to the catalogue. Family 032 was renamed from 'Hodge and Kuga-Satake Results for All Projective K3 Surfaces' and its K3 part removed on 7 October (secondary coverage).
events.revisions: Paper dated 30 Sep 2026 (README); public release in openai/math 6 Oct 2026; catalogue entry dated 6 Oct 2026; family renamed and K3 part removed on or about 7 Oct 2026 (history.md withdrawals; secondary coverage for the family change).
events.delivers: Per the catalogue quote and secondary coverage: the rational Hodge conjecture for complex CM abelian varieties (all dimensions and codimensions, per secondary coverage of Theorem 1.1). Through Milne's theorems (cited in the catalogue as the route): the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic, and the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields. These consequences are conditional on the CM result and on Milne's theorems as stated in Milne's papers. I did not read the paper PDF, so the theorem statement is from secondary coverage.
events.remains: The Hodge conjecture for non-CM abelian varieties and for general varieties; the non-rational (integral) Hodge conjecture; the general Hodge standard conjecture; Conjectures A/B, C, D in general.
events.doubts: (1) Unrefereed; no independent mathematician's assessment of the Hodge result found. (2) Catalogue marks Family 032 as not Lean-formalized (CONTENTS.md). (3) OpenAI's README: 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues.' (4) The same release withdrew three manuscripts on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error in a Weil-classes argument that two dependent papers relied on; the withdrawal notice (history.md) names three other papers, not this one, but a secondary report says the family's K3 part was removed; the claim that the CM core remains intact is secondary-source only. (5) Press coverage (The Information, 17 Sep 2026, citing one anonymous source) said staff expected to 'crack the Hodge Conjecture', which is a broader claim than the released manuscript. (6) Sutherland (MIT), quoted by Scientific American on 8 Oct 2026: 'we should expect some of the proofs to contain mistakes, possibly serious ones'. These are signals; the weight is for the later pass.
events.direction: Claims a proof of the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, cutting toward the conjectured direction for that class; claims, via Milne, the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic (cutting toward the conjectured direction for that class). It does not address the general statement.

events.what_happened: Only 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) addresses this. Its Corollary cc:standard claims two things for an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field K. First, for every prime l different from char(K), numerical and l-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A. Second, for every rational ample divisor class h and every 0 <= r <= g/2, the rational symmetric form (x,y) -> (-1)^r deg(x y h^{g-2r}) on the primitive kernel P_h^r(A)_Q is positive definite after extension to R. The text calls the second part the Hodge standard conjecture for l-adic cohomology of abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic. The proof re-applies Milne's Theorem 3.3 of Milne 2002 ('Polarizations and Grothendieck's standard conjectures'), read with Theorem 2.1, Milne's addendum and the 1999 addenda, with the Hodge-type hypothesis supplied by the paper's CM theorem.
events.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-September-30-2026, Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-September-30-2026, Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-September-30-2026
events.delivers: The Hodge standard conjecture (positivity of the form on primitive algebraic classes, modulo numerical equivalence) for abelian varieties over algebraically closed fields in all characteristics, and Conjecture D (numerical = homological equivalence) for abelian varieties, stated with the l-adic homological equivalence for every l different from the characteristic. The problem's list records Wikipedia's status note for D as the Clozel case for infinitely many primes l; this manuscript states the claim for every prime l different from the characteristic, so the judge should check that comparison. Not addressed: Conjectures A and B (Lefschetz type) and Conjecture C (Kunneth type) for any variety, and Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties. The manuscript does not claim to settle the full bullet.
events.remains: Conjectures A, B and C for all smooth projective varieties, and for abelian varieties (not addressed). Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties.
events.doubts: The corollary's correctness depends on Milne's proof and the two cited addenda, which I did not read. The text does not discuss Conjectures A, B or C at all. The abstract says 'the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic', while the corollary states the positivity for l-adic cohomology; I read this as the same claim, stated with l-adic cohomology. No step is flagged as sketched.; conditional on: Milne's Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 2.1 of Milne 2002 (Annals of Mathematics), read with Milne's author addendum to the 2002 paper and the 1999 addenda (both externally hosted at jmilne.org; not in the repository). The Hodge-type hypothesis is supplied by the paper's own CM theorem. The text says this is a re-application of Milne's proof with the same Hodge hypothesis, not a new argument.
events.direction: proves the Hodge standard conjecture and Conjecture D for abelian varieties (all characteristics)

disputes.summary: Press coverage blurs what was released. The Information (17 Sep 2026, citing one anonymous source) said staff expected to soon 'crack the Hodge Conjecture'; Gizmodo's article describes OpenAI as trying to solve it. The released manuscript is the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties only. Secondary outlets also describe a result on 'the Hodge standard conjecture' that is in fact the catalogue's consequence via Milne, not a claim in the manuscript's title. Altman's reported statements (first, second and fourth results have Lean proofs; Hodge does not) come from secondary coverage; the catalogue confirms only that Family 032 is not formalized.

The Wikipedia article (frozen Jan 2024) dates Ancona's fourfold result to 2020. The arXiv record shows the first public version on 8 June 2018; the published version is in Inventiones. The Hodge-type fourfold result is dated here by its first public written argument, per the rule.

The OpenAI CM family is dated 30 September 2026 in the README and folder name, and 6 October 2026 in the catalogue. The first public appearance is 6 October; the paper's self-date is recorded in the event.

Agugliaro's range of g: the arXiv abstract page (v2, fetched) says g >= 5; the v2 HTML abstract and the EMS page say g >= 4; a search snippet said g > 4 for the published version. Not resolved; see doubts on agugliaro-2024.
Ancona-Marmora Theorem 1.4 renders the modulus as '44' in the HTML; the abstract says modulo 4, so this is treated as a rendering error. Unverified against the PDF.

The withdrawn-manuscript notices (history.md) name three withdrawn papers, none of them the CM Hodge manuscript. A secondary report says the family was renamed and its K3 part removed, and that the CM core remains intact; OpenAI's own changelog could not be read in full, and the CM manuscript PDF could not be decoded, so the CM family's current text is not verified.

Milne's 2001 v1 claimed the Hodge standard conjecture for all smooth projective varieties conditional on the Tate conjecture; v3 and the Annals version restrict to abelian varieties. Recorded as a scope change in milne-2001.

Lieberman's 1968 contribution is described differently by the Wikipedia article (Conjecture D over C for dimension at most four and for abelian varieties) and by snippets (the Lefschetz standard conjecture for abelian varieties). Unresolved without the original paper.

summary: Nothing has settled the standard conjectures in general since 26 January 2024, and every source I read still treats them as open. What has happened is a run of partial results, mostly for abelian varieties and their powers, plus one large unrefereed claim. Best-established partial results: Agugliaro's explicit abelian-variety examples for the Hodge-type conjecture (arXiv 30 Jan 2024; Documenta Mathematica, published 19 Jan 2026) and his 2025 powers-of-threefolds result; Foster's Lefschetz results for Kummer-type hyper-Kahler varieties (2023 and a conditional 2025 result). Newer, unrefereed or withdrawn: Broe (arXiv 19 Aug 2026) proves the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields and, with Ancona, Kahn and Lieberman, claims to 'complete the proof of the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds' (the claim is restricted to fourfolds and rests on Markman and Ancona; no outside engagement found; two Li preprints cite it). Li (10 Sep 2026) claims Tate and standard conjecture D on powers of abelian fourfolds over finite fields; v2 was withdrawn on 8 Oct 2026. Shimizu (Zenodo 16 Aug 2025; Preprints.org 17 Sep 2025, unrefereed, self-described working draft) claims all four standard conjectures and the Rational Hodge conjecture; I found no engagement. The largest AI-linked event is OpenAI's release of 6 Oct 2026 (repository openai/math, 722 manuscripts, 719 after withdrawals): its manuscript dated 30 Sep 2026 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties; its catalogue lists the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic and the Tate conjecture over finite fields as consequences via Milne's theorems. The catalogue says Family 032 is not Lean-formalized, OpenAI says some unformalized results 'could have issues', and a sibling set of three papers was withdrawn on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error in a Weil-classes argument. No outside mathematician's assessment of the CM result was found; Sutherland's public comment was general. AI involvement, by source: (a) Broe's paper discloses that an unnamed large language model suggested the strategy the proof turns on (the 'stabilization' idea) after the author asked it to try Markman's results on Theorem 1.1; the author says they developed, restructured and corrected the argument, and the source names no model, so I recorded it as described; (b) Li's acknowledgements credit OpenAI Codex with exploration of proof strategies and proof auditing, and I did not read the body to judge whether it is load-bearing; (c) OpenAI's own README says the vast majority of release results came from an unreleased internal model with about three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute per result on average, and the CM paper is authored by 'OpenAI'. Pre-2024 events are dated by their first arXiv or publication record; I did not read full texts for most of them, and I set none_found true only where what I read named no system. Close calls: (1) whether Broe's 'completion' counts as the problem resolved (it is for abelian fourfolds only, so it cuts against the bullet's general statement); (2) whether the OpenAI CM claim should count, given that it is unrefereed, not formalized, and relies on Milne's theorems for its consequences; (3) whether an unnamed model's suggested idea, recorded as described, should count as AI involvement in the result.
competing_reading: Reading the Broe paper as a resolution: its Corollary 1.2 says that together with Lieberman and Ancona, the standard conjectures are complete for abelian fourfolds, and the author checked every statement. Against that: the bullet asks about all smooth projective varieties and Broe's result covers one dimension of one class. Reading the OpenAI CM result as a substantive advance on the standard conjectures: its catalogue entry derives the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic via Milne's theorems, which are conditional on the CM Hodge conjecture the manuscript claims to prove. Against that: the manuscript is unrefereed and not Lean-formalized, family-level errors have already been found in the same release, and the Milne derivation depends on the same unverified argument. Reading the Li result as moving standard conjecture D on powers of fourfolds: the abstract says it does; but v2 is withdrawn, its D statement says it follows from Broe's theorem, and so it does not stand independently of Broe. Reading the Shimizu claim as a resolution: only if its proof survives expert review, and no engagement is on record.
what_would_settle_it: For Broe: a referee report or an expert note checking the Markman reduction, the use of Ancona's exotic-class analysis and Kahn's theorem, and the AI-suggested 'stabilization' step; and the arXiv v2 or publication, if any. For OpenAI's CM Hodge result: the paper's Theorem 1.1 statement and proof read by algebraic geometers, a Lean formalization (absent per the catalogue), and a published OpenAI changelog entry saying whether the family changed after the 7 Oct withdrawals. For the standard conjectures' general status: Conjectures B, C and D and the Hodge-type statement for varieties beyond abelian varieties and K3 squares, none of which is in view in any source I read. For Shimizu: an expert engagement with the Preprints.org text, which I could not open. For Agugliaro's range of g: the arXiv v1 and v2 PDFs, and the Documenta Mathematica PDF.

event.what_happened: Agugliaro, Examples for the standard conjecture of Hodge type, arXiv:2401.17445 (v1 30 Jan 2024; v2 13 Nov 2025). Constructs, for each prime p and each integer g (see note), infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p satisfying the Hodge-type standard conjecture, using Honda-Tate theory and a theorem of Ancona on rank-2 motives. The examples have Tate classes that are neither generated by divisors nor liftable to characteristic zero. Published Documenta Mathematica vol. 31 (2026), pp. 855-904, DOI 10.4171/DM/1057; EMS lists the published date as 19 January 2026.
event.revisions: v1 30 Jan 2024 (first public version, four days after the frozen revision); v2 13 Nov 2025 (current, accepted in Documenta Mathematica).
event.delivers: Instances: for each prime p and each g >= 4 (per the v2 HTML and the EMS abstract), infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p satisfying the Hodge-type standard conjecture. The arXiv abstract page I read gives g >= 5 instead; see doubts.
event.remains: The Hodge-type conjecture for all abelian varieties and all varieties; Conjectures B, C, D in general; the examples do not exhaust any class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published; EMS journal page lists 'Published' 19 January 2026, Vol. 31, No. 4

event.doubts: The range of g differs between sources: the arXiv abstract page (fetched) says g >= 5; the v2 HTML abstract and the EMS page say g >= 4 (the search snippet said g > 4 for the published version). Taken together I read g >= 4 as current, but this is unresolved. The construction is explicit (Honda-Tate); I did not verify it.
event.direction: Instances of the Hodge-type standard conjecture for a class of abelian varieties; cuts in the conjectured direction.
event.object: Infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g over the algebraic closure of F_p, for each prime p and each g in the stated range, built explicitly by Honda-Tate theory; they satisfy the Hodge-type standard conjecture and carry Tate classes not generated by divisors nor liftable to characteristic zero.

judgement.why: The statement names four conjectures (A/B, C, D, Hodge-type), each over all smooth projective varieties, so any result restricted to a class of varieties or one conjecture is a case. Broe's completion for abelian fourfolds is a case, unreviewed but by a serious method with no identified error, so credible; its disclosure says the model suggested the method and the stabilization idea the proof turns on, which is mathematics in the result, so assisted rather than none. The OpenAI CM manuscript (recorded twice, as openai-cm-hodge-2026 and openai-math-032) gives the Hodge standard conjecture and D for abelian varieties in all characteristics via Milne: a case, unreviewed, doubtful because of the same-release sign-error withdrawals, and generated, since OpenAI is the sole author. Agugliaro 2024 (30 Jan 2024, four days after the snapshot) constructs infinitely many abelian varieties per dimension satisfying the Hodge-type conjecture, not a finite check, so it is a case, digested through Documenta. Foster 2025 and Truong are conditional on open conjectures, so none. Ancona-Marmora's mod-4 signature is a weaker form, so variant. Li's codex credit (strategy exploration, auditing) is too thin to count, and both Li papers are withdrawn anyway. Shimizu has several F10 signals together and is not_credible.
judgement.doubts: openai-cm-hodge-2026 and openai-math-032 are one manuscript split into two events; both are answered alike. For the CM paper the per-family generation procedure is not stated in the record (the 032 quote says the CM Hodge work was an exception to the fixed procedure); I took OpenAI's sole authorship as enough for generated. Broe's assisted versus generated was close: the model proposed the method, but the author says they developed, restructured and corrected it. Agugliaro 2024's case-versus-instances call was close: infinitely many explicit examples rather than a complete class.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
